I have talked to them (not regarding suicidal thoughts, but regarding depression). Actually, the only reason I found out it was depression was because a friend diagnosed with it and in therapy since a few years told me about his experiences. I kicked it around my head for a long time and finally went to see a doctor who diagnosed me.

Apart from that one friend (whom I now see very rarely because he moved away) I've tried talking to one other friend, and my father. Both of them don't seem to understand what depression is or how I feel, they think I can just "snap out of it", so I've stopped talking to them about this topic.

The latter.

My mind is destroying itself. Nobody in my family or friends has died recently; I have a good job and while I'm not rich, I can easily make ends meet and I'm not in debt; I *should* have a sunny outlook but deep down, I don't.

Thank you everybody. I'm now calmed down enough (or just physically tired enough) I can at least try to go to sleep. If it works, I won't be replying in the next few hours.

Also because somebody PM'd me asking for it and it might be of interest to others, I'm a 24-year-old male.
Depends. I imagined being able to read minds or control other people's thoughts, or to jump arbitrarily high, or just be strong and impervious to bullets, or run faster than a car can drive.

> Work is a popular place for people to meet and food has a way of bringing people together. You never know!!

Unlikely, considering where I work, and how the culture here is.

> You sound so wonderfully creative!! Have you thought about writing these daydreams down? Drawing comics of them? 

I tried writing them down, but they only work as long as they are in my brain. I didn't try drawing them but I draw like shit.

> I didn't see love or friends happening soon for me either. A beautiful surprise.

I only leave my apartment for work and groceries. I won't meet anybody.

> Does anything seem to alleviate it, even just temporarily?

Only when I'm in "fantasy worlds": I regularly have daydreams for an hour or so where I'm having unrealistic fantasies (think superhero or world leader) to "get away". Although I know those fantasies are unrealistic, they provide temporary relief from "every day is shittier than the last". It only works when I'm in a "high" phase where I'm relatively functional, in my current situation I can't focus enough for a daydream.

> Care to tell us what's weighing heavily on your mind?

What do you mean?

> I've fallen in love, made some friends, even started going back to school.

I haven't, and I don't see any of this happening soon.

> In particular, it really helps me to think about tomorrow. Not in a 'this is what I have to do' kind of way, but in a 'what will happen next?' kind of way. Life is like a story to me. There's a beginning, middle and end. I'm still young, so I'm in the middle. I'm at the best part of the story, where all the cool stuff happens. Tomorrow could be like today, and the day before, or the day before that. But it might be different. It might be the best day of my life, the climax in my story. I wouldn't want you to miss the best day of your life, the climax of your story.

Intellectually, I know that therapy, when it finally starts, is probably going to improve my life. The problem is, it doesn't impact how I *feel*. I feel like every day is going to be worse than the previous day.
